newsitem.title: USA: DNC returns $107,000 to Native Americans.
newsitem.headline: DNC returns $107,000 to Native Americans.

text.p: The Democratic National Committee said Thursday it had returned $107,000 donated by Native Americans because the origin of the money was unclear and tribal leaders believed it was linked to a favourable hearing on their land claims.
The Cheyenne-Arapaho Indians of Oklahoma contributed to the DNC last year hoping their support would result in Clinton administration action on the return of tribal lands.

"First, we could not clarify from the tribe which tribal fund the donation came from, and second, we wanted to be clear that there is no linkage between a donation and a fair hearing on the tribe's request for the return of tribal lands," the DNC said in a statement.
"After several days of discussing the donation with the tribal leadership, we are not confident that the money did not come from their welfare fund," the DNC said.
The statement noted that there appeared to be a link in the minds of the tribe's members between the donation and the hearing on return of tribal lands.
"That is not the case, and we cannot retain this money if they believe that to be so," the DNC added.
Tribal leaders have been seeking the return of 7,500 acres within their reservation taken by the federal government in 1869 for a military fort, Fort Reno.
